subject: Clarifying SOC 2 coverage: epoch / point-in-time inclusivity
messages:
From: Caroline Reed <caroline.reed@certaudit.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: soc2-audits@certaudit.com
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 Type II: inclusivity of boundary instants

Hi Alex,

Quick question as we prepare the SOC 2 Type II coverage work for AcmePay: when you say the report covers the period 2025-10-01 through 2026-09-30, does Redwood treat the start/end as inclusive instants (i.e., events that occur at 00:00:00 on 2025-10-01 or at 23:59:59.999 on 2026-09-30 count)?

A couple of clarifying sub-questions:
- Do you operate on UTC for audit evidence cutoffs, or are there services where local timezones apply?
- For point-in-time artifacts (snapshots, backups), are those taken at EOD (23:59:59 UTC) or sometimes earlier (e.g., 23:30) and still considered representative?

If you have a short artifact (manifest or example timestamp) showing how you label snapshots that would be really helpful.

Thanks,
Caroline
Caroline Reed
Senior Auditor, CertAudit
caroline.reed@certaudit.com

Attachment: none in this message
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Reed <caroline.reed@certaudit.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II: inclusivity of boundary instants

Hi Caroline — thanks for the clear questions. Short answer: we treat the inclusive period as full calendar days in UTC, and we provide both end-of-day snapshots plus event-level logs to support any point-in-time assertions. More detail below and attaching a small manifest for examples.

Answers:
- Inclusive endpoints: yes — the report period 2025-10-01 through 2026-09-30 is inclusive. Events with timestamps that fall on 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC are in scope, as are events up to 2026-09-30 23:59:59.999 UTC.
- Timezone: we normalize audit evidence to UTC for SOC reporting. Operational systems may record local timezones internally, but our evidence delivery (snapshots, manifests, logs) includes ISO 8601 UTC timestamps.
- Snapshot timing: primary evidence is an EOD UTC snapshot (usually between 23:58–23:59:59 UTC) for stateful systems. For some streaming/event systems we provide event-level extracts with millisecond resolution. If a snapshot was taken earlier (e.g., 23:30 UTC) due to maintenance, we flag that in the manifest and include a matching event log extract.

I'm attaching a small manifest (log-manifest.csv) and a draft bridge letter that uses precise language for inclusivity. Neha / Priyom — can you confirm the wording below (especially the note about flagged early snapshots) and, if OK, confirm we can publish the bridge letter to AcmePay's auditor?

Best,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II: inclusivity of boundary instants

Alex / Caroline — confirmed. A few precise points from the compliance team for the bridge letter:

1) Coverage window: Redwood Inference confirms the SOC 2 Type II reporting period of 2025-10-01 through 2026-09-30 is inclusive of the entire days in UTC (i.e., the period includes 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC through 2026-09-30 23:59:59.999 UTC).

2) Evidence semantics:
   - State snapshots: primary point-in-time evidence is provided as end-of-day snapshots normalized to UTC. Typical snapshot timestamps are 23:58:00–23:59:59 UTC.
   - Event logs: where event-level fidelity is required, we deliver event extracts that include ISO 8601 UTC timestamps with millisecond precision.
   - Early snapshot exceptions: if we take a snapshot earlier than EOD for operational reasons, we include a manifest entry with the actual timestamp and a corresponding log extract covering the gap.

3) Sample artifacts: attached is a short snapshot-sample.tsv (small extract) and our bridge-letter-draft.docx; the latter includes the exact phrasing we recommend for auditor consumption.

Caroline — if that looks good we can sign the bridge letter and include the manifest + sample artifact for your review.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
